newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine must work to develop stock market--SEC.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine must work to develop stock market--SEC.

text.p: Ukraine has all the raw ingredients needed for a stock market but must work hard to make it function, the head of the Securities and Exchange Commission said on Thursday.

"The state of the stock market is such that all the elements exist for a developed market, such as organisation, investment company and regulators," Oleg Mozgovoy told a stock markets conference. "But we can also say the market is not developed."
Investors say Ukraine has yet to create a central depositary, registration system, custodial services and clearing and settlement systems.

Share trading is conducted on the Ukrainian Stock Exchange and its 29 affiliates, on the Kiev-based PFTS OTC Stock Trading System, the Kyiv International Stock Exchange and the Donetsk Stock Exchange in eastern Ukraine. Some trading also takes place on the Ukrainian Interbank Currency Exchange (UICE).
Thin trading and a general lack of transparency for prices and capital mean Ukraine's stock market is still embryonic.

About 80 percent of all trading takes place on the one-year-old OTC market, which lists about 130 companies. The record turnover is $4.5 million over one week. Turnover on the Ukrainian Stock Exchange is estimated at $200,000 per week.
Prague-based Wood and Company has started an index to track the top 15 companies listed on the OTC stock trading system.
"Investors are the people living here," Mosgovoy said. "We want to see them invest, but there is a very low understanding of this process."
